The observed patterns are consistent across data subsets but without the interaction of area and biome. On oceanic islands with endemics (n = 69), area remains the strongest predictor (β = 0.32, P < 0.001, R2 = 0.38; Extended Data Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 5). Among islands rich in SIE (>5% of native richness; n = 96), SIE richness increases with area (β = 0.36, P < 0.001, R2 = 0.66) and increases marginally with sampling completeness (β = 0.16, P = 0.02) (Extended Data Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 5). These results parallel global patterns of vascular plant endemism on islands47. The mid-latitudinal peak in bee species richness2, seen on islands predominantly in the Northern Hemisphere, does not translate into increased bee endemism. Rather, bee endemism is greatest in the tropics (Extended Data Fig. 5). Patterns for AE are broadly similar. Across islands hosting AEs (n = 217) area was again the main predictor and interacted with biome (Supplementary Table 5). However, AE–area slopes were consistent across tropical, temperate, and Mediterranean-type biomes, with only desert islands showing a significantly lower rate than tropical islands (Δ = 0.35, P = 0.01; Supplementary Table 6). Isolation (distance from mainland) is non-significant (β = −0.04, P = 0.48) and sampling completeness is also included as a significant effect, suggesting that islands with high numbers of AEs are also the best studied (β = 0.14, P = 0.01). Additionally, there is a significant positive effect of elevation (β = 0.18, P = 0.01) suggesting that topographically complex islands support a greater diversity of endemics at the archipelago scale (Extended Data Fig. 6).

It has been revealed that A model predicting SIE from overall native richness alone reveals a clear correlation (R2 = 0.44) and improved significantly with the inclusion of biome (ΔR2 = 0.15, χ2 = 33.1, P < 0.001; Supplementary Table 8). Although adding the interaction term yields a significant model improvement (ΔR2 = 0.02, χ2 = 8.15, P = 0.04), post hoc pairwise comparisons reveal no significant differences in slopes between biomes after correcting for multiple testing (Supplementary Table 8). This indicates a practically uniform global rate of increasing SIE with richness but with distinct baseline shifts; specifically, Mediterranean-type islands support significantly fewer baseline SIEs than all other biomes (Extended Data Fig. 7). Conversely, for AEs (R2 = 0.55), the full interaction model results in the best fit (ΔR2 = 0.14, χ2 = 72.54, P < 0.001; Extended Data Fig. 7 and Supplementary Table 8), demonstrating that the rate endemic species accumulate with increasing richness is biome-dependent. Pairwise comparisons indicate that the slope for Mediterranean-type biomes (0.42 ± 0.10) is significantly flatter than in desert (0.83 ± 0.12, P = 0.02), tropical (0.96 ± 0.03, P < 0.001) and temperate (0.75 ± 0.06, P = 0.01) biomes, indicating a partial decoupling between richness and AE (Supplementary Table 9). Although Mediterranean-type islands generally support fewer AEs than expected across the richness gradient, the Canary Islands stand out as an exception, showing high AE richness consistent with their high overall richness, although probably enhanced by their relative isolation from the primary Mediterranean source pool (Extended Data Fig. 6). This divergence also highlights that the AE model probably captures more ancient diversification compared with the SIE model48,49. This partial decoupling contrasts with vascular plants, for which the richest islands also tend to host the highest numbers of endemic species, particularly in the case of large tropical islands9. Our results are consistent with previous macroecological studies50, suggesting that the relationship between richness and endemism is not simple and varies among taxa.

Together, these findings reveal that bee endemism is concentrated on large tropical islands and certain oceanic archipelagos rather than in areas of peak species richness globally. New Guinea and Madagascar stand out for supporting both high numbers and high proportions of endemic species. By contrast, certain other island systems, including the Caribbean, the Philippines and the Hawaiian islands, are characterized by only a high proportion of endemics. This apparent divergence between patterns of richness and endemism suggests a distinction between the factors structuring island assembly attributable to colonization and evolutionary diversification in bees. Wet, humid tropical conditions, combined with greater isolation of many oceanic tropical islands, present environmental barriers to bee colonization2. Therefore, successful colonizers are presented with greater ecological opportunity, and this can lead to high in situ diversification1. These patterns suggest distinct evolutionary histories: high endemism in Madagascar probably reflects multiple independent radiations51, whereas in other systems single radiations account for high proportions of endemism, such as Palaeorhiza in New Guinea52, Hylaeus (Nesoprosopis) in the Hawaiian archipelago6 and Lasioglossum (Homalictus) across Pacific islands such as Samoa and Fiji53,54. Conversely, the factors that support high richness in Mediterranean-type islands are likely to include: (1) the adaptation to arid environments; but also (2) frequent arrivals from nearby continental source pools, providing sufficient gene flow to inhibit in situ diversification and thus result in lower endemism55. Globally, bees provide evidence that endemism, and by extension extinction risk, is not inextricably linked to overall species richness, often diverging into regions of high endemism but low richness or high richness with low endemism56.

Building on these findings, we additionally examine how plant diversity, as a potential biotic driver, covaries with bee richness, given that bees depend strongly on flowering plants for food and nesting resources22,24. Across the 175 islands for which we have both angiosperm richness data and native bee richness, we observe a positive correlation: angiosperm richness alone explains 49% of variation in bee richness across islands (R2 = 0.49), a relationship that persists after accounting for island area and isolation (β = 0.64, P < 0.001; Fig. 5a and Supplementary Table 10). The slope of the relationship between angiosperm and bee richness is largely consistent across biomes (likelihood ratio test: χ2 = 7.02, P = 0.06). However, temperate islands show a slightly steeper relationship compared with the tropical baseline (β = 0.55, P = 0.015; Fig. 5a and Supplementary Table 10). Additionally, we observe differences from the baseline in total supported bee richness in Mediterranean-type islands: they support 5.6 times more bee species than tropical islands at equivalent plant richness, area and isolation (P < 0.001; Fig. 5b and Supplementary Table 11).

Points are coloured by biome (desert, tropical, temperate and Mediterranean-type; boreal islands were excluded owing to small sample size (n = 3 islands)). The solid line represents the fitted mean regression from a mixed-effects model including angiosperm richness and biome, with archipelago as a random intercept, with dashed lines indicating 95% confidence intervals. Native angiosperm richness was evaluated using a two-sided t-test with Satterthwaite’s approximation for degrees of freedom (β = 0.60, 95% confidence interval [0.36, 0.84], t(126) = 5.00, P = 1.89 × 10−6). b, Bee species richness for each island (n = 175 islands) adjusted to the global mean angiosperm richness, area and isolation. Violins show the distribution of adjusted richness within each biome (ordered by increasing median), overlaid with box plots and individual islands (jittered points). Values below box plots show the estimated fold change in adjusted bee richness relative to tropical islands (Supplementary Table 10).

In a recent development, the relationship between angiosperm and bee richness probably reflects a combination of shared biogeographic drivers, such as area and climate, as well as ecological dependence, although the contribution of these factors cannot be separated here. However, the markedly higher baseline bee richness in Mediterranean-type islands at equivalent angiosperm richness is consistent with the hypothesis that temperature seasonality promotes bee specialization57. Seasonal climates can promote bee specialization through temporal resource partitioning while perhumid tropical systems, despite higher plant richness, may present ecological filters that limit bee diversity. Therefore, capturing more detailed information on the complex networks that wild bees form with native plants, and how they vary with island isolation and reduced colonization events, is crucial for developing more complete models of island biodiversity58,59 (reviewed in ref. 1). Yet recent evidence highlights that flowering plant communities may be reliant on bee pollinators when bee richness is comparatively low60. Consequently, we should not expect a simple, predictable relationship between plant and bee richness across islands of differing biomes, isolation and area.

Recent findings suggest that our study demonstrates that islands account for a substantial share of global bee diversity, including many species that evolved on islands and are endemic. We find that species richness and endemism are partly disconnected, highlighting that these two metrics capture distinct aspects of insular bee diversity. Richness peaks in mid-latitude, Mediterranean-type islands in the Northern Hemisphere, whereas peak endemism occurs in large tropical islands, with these differences being strongest for oceanic islands. These patterns are further supported by the biome-dependent relationship between angiosperm and bee richness, showing that although floral richness is a strong predictor of bee diversity across islands, it does not fully account for the differences in bee richness observed among biomes. Only a small percentage of island bee species have been assessed for extinction risk29,30, and this risk is probably tied to evolutionary distinctiveness rather than richness55. Therefore, our results suggest that conserving bees on islands requires prioritization of areas of unique evolutionary history, from large continental fragments such as Madagascar to remote oceanic archipelagos like the Hawaiian islands, over species richness alone.

Bees are particularly well suited as a model taxon for studying island biogeographical dynamics. They are pivotal pollinators that are closely linked to plant reproduction and ecosystem functioning22, and represent a taxonomically discrete group with an increasing availability of distributional and phylogenetic data. However, much remains to be explored in understanding the mechanisms behind the patterns of colonization and speciation, and the potential for newly introduced discoveries. The increasing availability of molecular phylogenies opens up new research avenues for addressing the evolutionary history of bees27. Combined with detailed distribution and trait data61, these resources make it possible to reconstruct historical patterns of colonization, extinction and speciation on islands. With the baseline established here, we lay the foundation for understanding the colonization, diversification and vulnerability of insect diversity on islands more broadly.

In a recent development, we verified the presence of bees on islands on the basis of information available on Discover Life (https://www.discoverlife.org/) and more detailed and recently updated information, notably, for type locality and collection event data, extracted from source files for that resource21. These expert-vetted lists were filtered for island records and joined with spatial data to align species presence with island identifiers. The checklist data on Discover Life were collected from a variety of sources, including taxonomic revisions, primary species descriptions (including synonyms), verified human observations, and undigitized museum records. To avoid complications from historical boundary changes, species were recorded at the current state or country level. The data are available online as a matrix at the country level, with species-specific details provided for finer geographic scales. For further details on how the checklists were sourced see ref. 4. For islands not clearly associated with a specific country or state/province, additional sources were used to confirm species presence based on the broader political region. We then cross-referenced specimens with island-specific faunal checklists from the published literature; for example, when a species was known only from an archipelago we tried to determine its presence on specific islands within the archipelago. These included studies from Abd al Kuri and Socotra from the Socotra Archipelago65, the Azores including Corvo, Faial, Flores, Graciosa, Pico, Santa Maria, São Jorge, São Miguel and Terceira66, Balearic Islands including Ibiza, Mallorca and Menorca67, Bonaire68, Cabo Verde including Boa Vista, Brava, Sal, Santiago, Santo Antão, São Nicolau and São Vicente69, Cuba and East Grand Bahama70, Fiji52,71, Isla de Juventud72, Juan Fernández Islands73, Madeira Archipelago including Madeira, Porto Santo, and Deserto Grande and Selvagens Islands including Selvagem Grande74 and Madagascar75,76. European island checklists were extracted from the latest checklists for European species from Reverte et al.77 and included Åland islands, Great Britain, Ireland, Iceland, Faroe Islands, Malta, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, Crete, Cyprus and Isle of Man. We also included validated (Research Grade) iNaturalist records (up to December 2024) for all islands available from the initial checklists. Although these entries provide valuable data, a degree of taxonomic doubt remains, consequently, they have been labelled as uncertain within the final dataset pending further validation. The checklists for the Greek islands of Corfu and Rhodes were expanded with records from Rhodes78,79, Corfu80 and the personal collection of T. J. Wood. Recent additions to Corsica and Sardinia were also added81, as were the latest checklists of the Canary Islands82. Finally, the bee fauna of Tasmania was significantly adjusted due to recent taxonomic work on the Parasphecodes subgenus83. Names were cleaned using the synonym lists from Orr et al.4 and Dorey et al.84. In some cases, it was not possible to separate archipelago-level data into island records and some archipelagos were therefore retained in the dataset (for example, for the Solomon Islands).

To classify non-native species and calculate final island native species richness, we used Russo85 as a baseline, complemented by existing checklist information and expert opinion from J.S.A. Using the checklists, we calculated three measures of wild bee richness and endemism on islands. They included: (1) native species richness, calculated as the total number of unique native species included in the checklist for each island (or archipelago, as the case may be); (2) single-island endemism, calculated as the total number of species on the checklist only known from that island; (3) AE, calculated as the total number of species found only on that archipelago: this includes all SIEs.

Using the above checklists, we extracted a spatially explicit database of islands by matching the names from the checklist to those found in the global islands (greater than 1 km2 in area) database of Sayre et al.63. We extracted a vector shapefile of all islands for which we had any wild bee checklist information. In most cases we endeavoured to associate each checklist with a single island entity. In cases where a single name from the bee database is associated with multiple land masses, we extracted all the landmasses for subsequent calculations (for example, Sao Tome and Principe, Saint Vincent and Grenadines, Wallis and Futuna, Antigua and Barbuda, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and Solomon Islands). Duplicate island names and spatial mismatches were checked manually. Following this we harmonized the island names with the islands included in the Global Inventory of Floras and Traits (GIFT) database and extracted information on island area, isolation (distance to mainland), island category (oceanic, fragment or continental), archipelago and richness of angiosperms from GIFT (for more detail, see ref. 20). Islands in the GIFT database were categorized by geological origin into oceanic (volcanic islands and atolls), continental shelf (land-bridge), and complex origin/continental fragments. Categorizing islands into three discrete types is a necessary simplification. Certain cases, such as the tectonic uplift of Cyprus or continental fragments such as Rhodes, New Caledonia and Seram that underwent periods of total submergence, represent intermediate states where biological isolation was prioritized over strict geological origin. Specifically, a lack of historical land-bridge connections was used to classify islands as oceanic in type. Of the final 305 islands, there were 207 oceanic islands, 25 fragment islands and 73 continental islands (see Supplementary Table 12 for a full breakdown by biome).

According to recent reports, species distribution data for 350,707 vascular plant species across 1,967 islands and 1,010 mainland regions were taken from Schrader et al.9 and then associated with islands for which we have bee species checklists. These data were originally sourced from the GIFT v.3.2 database using the R package GIFT86 and are taxonomically standardized according to the World Checklist of Vascular Plants9,20. In the few cases where we had bee checklist data for an island or archipelago that did not correspond to an island or archipelago in the GIFT database—for example, data aggregated at archipelago level in one but not the other—we calculated area and isolation directly from the aforementioned spatial map of islands63 and island-specific literature was used to determine island category and archipelago.

Recent findings suggest that we incorporated additional island-level environmental information by overlaying our island shapefile with a spatial global shapefile of ecoregions62, which is an patch of the original WWF biogeographical regionalization of Olson et al.87. This dataset provides a globally standardized classification of terrestrial ecoregions, biomes and biogeographic realms, and was selected because it offers consistent, GIS-based borders that explicitly include oceanic islands, allowing reproducible assignment of islands based solely on spatial overlap. Although developed as a general terrestrial biodiversity classification rather than for specific taxa, the underlying climatic, floristic and evolutionary discontinuities that define these realms are expected to also be relevant for bees, whose distributions are closely tied to vegetation structure and climatic regimes. Each island was assigned to a terrestrial biome and biogeographic realm using the intersect function from the R package sf (v1.0-2188). Biome classifications were aggregated into broader categories (boreal, desert, Mediterranean, temperate and tropical) for comparative purposes (Supplementary Table 13) and the final selected biome was the dominant biome found on the island. Realm classifications were one of Afrotropic, Australasia, Indomalaya, Nearctic, Neotropic, Oceania and Palaearctic. This allowed for consistent ecological context across islands and facilitated analyses of native bee richness by biome type and realm.

We also calculated additional isolation metrics by computing the edge-to-edge distance (km) from each study island to the nearest landmass across three size classes (>1 km2, >1,000 km2 and >10,000 km2) and the cumulative surrounding land area (km2) within buffers of 10 km, 100 km and 1,000 km around each island. To do this, we combined our global island database with a global continental layer from rnaturalearth v1.0.189. We tested correlations (r > 0.7) among all isolation variables prior to model fitting (Supplementary Fig. 1). We selected distance to the nearest landmass >1,000 km2 and the total land area within the 10 km buffer to represent isolation, alongside distance to mainland (km), in the final set of variables with which we conducted model selection. Climate data were extracted from bioclimatic rasters from the CHELSA v2.190 with a resolution of 30 arcsec. The variables included annual mean temperature (BIO1), temperature seasonality (BIO4; defined as the standard deviation of monthly mean temperatures multiplied by 100), annual precipitation (BIO12), and precipitation seasonality (BIO15; defined as the coefficient of variation of monthly precipitation). Local elevation metrics were extracted for each island using the elevatr package (v0.99.1)91. Climate variables were averaged for each island and elevation was recorded as the elevational range of each island.

Industry observers note that to ensure comparability and ecological and biogeographical relevance, we limited our final dataset to islands with a minimum area of 5 km2 and located at least 1 km from the mainland. These thresholds helped to remove islands with high edge effects, and limited habitat heterogeneity, while ensuring a meaningful biogeographical break from the mainland.

In a recent development, to explore global patterns of bee sampling on islands we used the BeeBDC protocol outlined in Dorey et al.84 to extract all global records of bees on islands. Specifically, we downloaded all records of Anthophila from Global Biodiversity Information Facility92, Atlas of Living Australia93 and iDigBio. We corrected synonymous names as above using the synonym lists from Dorey et al.84 and Orr et al.4. As part of the cleaning process the data were subset to only include names of species found in the island checklist dataset, ensuring incorrect records of valid species unlikely to occur on the island were removed. To link bee occurrence records with islands spatially, we reprojected all coordinates to match the island shapefile and performed a spatial join, retaining only records intersecting island polygons defined in the checklist dataset. To ensure consistency between occurrence and checklist data, all species listed in the island checklists were added as supplementary records to the public database, standardizing species richness values across sources. The final dataset comprised 663,189 georeferenced records, which were subsequently used to assess sampling effort and spatial coverage across islands included in the analysis. This dataset was used to calculate a proxy for sampling effort and sampling completeness. To measure sampling completeness we calculated sampling coverage across islands using the Chao & Jost64 method via the coverage function in the iNEXT3D R package (v1.08)94. We used a species/island abundance (count of all occurrences per species per island) matrix of all records to estimate the proportion of the total individuals per island that belong to the observed species, using a non-parametric estimator that accounts for the frequency of rare species (singletons and doubletons). To account for large differences in sampling effort we additionally weighted coverage based on the total number of occurrence records, subsequently referred to as a sample-size-adjusted measure of sampling completeness.

We used the Discover Life global checklist through the BeeBDC tool84 as our baseline source for global bee species richness. To generate an estimate of mainland-only species richness, we excluded all species known to occur on islands by comparing with the above checklists and by removing all island-level records from the global checklist. The global checklist was also used to supplement endemism and island-only species data by filtering out species only recorded on islands from the checklist and cross-referencing with the island dataset. The mainland checklist was also used to test island occurrence patterns to create a binary classification of all species as either occurring or not occurring on islands.

Recent findings suggest that we used the island-level checklists to test the key predictors of species richness on islands. We fit a linear mixed-effects model using the lmer function from the lme4 R package (v1.1-37)95, with native species richness as the response variable. We log10-transformed native species richness after adding 1 to all values to accommodate islands with zero native bee species (n = 4) while preserving them in the analysis.

We constructed a full model including the full set of ecological predictors, and then tested all possible model subsets (dredge function, R package MuMIn v1.48.1196). In all models, log10-transformed island area and a measure of island isolation were retained as fixed effects because these variables represent the core predictions of island biogeography theory. We evaluated three alternative isolation metrics in separate full models: log10-transformed distance to the nearest mainland, log10-transformed distance to the nearest landmass exceeding 1,000 km2, and the surrounding land area in a 10 km buffer around the island.

The full model also included biome (5 categories), elevation range (log10), mean annual temperature (scaled), temperature seasonality (log10), annual precipitation (log10), precipitation seasonality (log10), island type (continental, fragment, or oceanic), and sampling completeness (sample-size-adjusted coverage, log10). We also evaluated an Area × Biome interaction and an Isolation × Biome interaction. We assessed collinearity among predictors using variance inflation factors (VIF; R package car, vif function97); mean annual temperature showed high collinearity with biome and other climate variables across all datasets (VIF > 5), and removing it from the full model brought all remaining predictors below this threshold. We therefore excluded mean annual temperature from the full model. Archipelago identity was included as a random intercept in all models to account for spatial non-independence among islands within the same archipelago and to allow baseline species richness to vary among archipelagos98. Models were fit by maximum likelihood and ranked by AICc; models with all three isolation-metric were then pooled into a single ranked set of models. When more than one model was within ΔAICc < 2, we selected the simplest model with the fewest degrees of freedom (Supplementary Table 4). The best-supported model included:.

log10(NativeSpeciesRichness)ij = β0 + β1 × log10(Area)ij + β2 × Biomeij + β3 × (log10(Area)ij × Biomeij) + β4 × log10(Isolation)ij + β5 × IslandTypeij + β6 × SamplingCompletenessij + uj + εij.

NativeSpeciesRichnessij = number of native bee species observed on island i in archipelago j.

Isolationij = distance to nearest mainland (km).

IslandTypeij = island type (continental, fragment, oceanic).

SamplingCompletenessij = sample-size-adjusted coverage.

β3 = interaction between log10(area) and biome.

β4 = effect of log10(isolation)β5 = effects of island type.

β6 = effect of sampling completeness.

uj = random intercept for archipelago j.

Sources indicate that the final model included the interaction between area and biome, indicating that the effect of area on species richness varies among biomes. Island type and sampling completeness were retained as fixed effects. Two island groups for which coverage could not be calculated were dropped from the final model (Wallis and Futuna, Pitcairn Islands, n = 303). We quantified variance explained by fixed effects alone using marginal R2 and using conditional R2 for variance explained by both fixed and random effects99. To compare species–area relationship slopes among biomes, we extracted biome-specific slopes and their standard errors from the variance–covariance matrix of fixed effects. We then tested for specific differences among biomes using pairwise comparisons of estimated marginal means for intercepts and estimated marginal trends for slopes (FDR correction100) using the emmeans package (v1.11.1)101. Model predictions and confidence intervals were generated using the fixed-effects design matrix and visualized using ggplot2 (v3.5.2)102. Finally, we fit the same best model for only oceanic and only continental and fragment islands, specifically to compare ISAR slopes among biomes of different island types.

Sources indicate that to explore the predictors of endemic species richness and its relationship with total species richness across islands, we used a model selection approach mirroring our richness analysis. We fit a series of linear mixed-effects models using the lmer function from the R package lme4 (v1.1-37)95. Collinearity among predictors was assessed the same way as for richness and mean annual temperature was also removed from all endemism full models.

Recent findings suggest that we focused on islands supporting at least one single-island endemic (SIE ≥ 1; n = 113 islands). In this subset of islands, all biomes are represented apart from boreal, as the boreal islands harboured no endemics. We used the same model fitting procedure as described for the native richness analysis. All models within ΔAICc < 2 are shown in Supplementary Table 7. The best-supported model included:.

log10(Endemism)ij = β0 + β1 × log10(Area)ij + β2 × Biomeij + β3 × (log10(Area)ij × Biomeij) + β4 × log10(TemperatureSeasonality)ij + β5 × log10(Isolation)ij + uj + εij.

Endemismij = number of single-island endemic bee species observed on island i in archipelago j.

TemperatureSeasonalityij = temperature seasonality.

Isolationij = distance to nearest landmass >1,000 km2.

β3 = interaction between log10(area) and biome.

β4 = effect of log10(temperature seasonality).

β5 = effect of log10(isolation).

uj = random intercept for archipelago j.

To assess the generality of endemism patterns, we repeated analyses on three subsets: (1) oceanic islands only (n = 69), where endemism is more probably driven by neo-endemic evolution rather than the retention of land-bridge palaeo-endemics; (2) endemic-rich islands (SIE > 5% of total richness; n = 96), focusing on systems where endemism is well-established. We also repeated all analyses for AEs (species endemic to entire archipelagos; AE ≥ 1; n = 217) to confirm patterns were robust across endemism definitions (Supplementary Tables 5 and  7). The archipelago-level approach captures archipelago-wide diversification processes while revealing which individual islands within archipelagos are endemism hotspots (see, for example, ref. 48). For the SIE ≥ 1 and oceanic island subsets, the variance of the archipelago random effect was estimated at zero; however, it was kept for consistency across all models.

Additionally, to formally test how the relationship between richness and endemism varies across biomes, we compared three nested models for SIEs and AEs:.

where endemism is predicted solely by richness: log10(SIE/AE) ~ log10(Richness) + (1|Archipelago);.

where biome adds information beyond richness: log10(SIE/AE) ~ log10(Richness) + Biome + (1|Archipelago); and.

where the slope of the effect of richness varies by biome: log10(SIE/AE) ~ log10(Richness) × Biome + (1|Archipelago).

Sources indicate that we compared these nested models sequentially using likelihood ratio tests. If including biome as a fixed effect significantly improves model fit, this indicates that islands with similar richness support different baseline levels of endemism depending on biome. If including the interaction between biome and richness improves model fit then the rate at which endemics accumulate with increasing richness also varies across biomes. We then tested for specific differences among biomes using pairwise comparisons of estimated marginal means for intercepts and estimated marginal trends for slopes (FDR correction100) using the emmeans package (V1.11.1)101.

Recent findings suggest that to assess the extent to which bee diversity tracks angiosperm diversity across islands, we fitted a linear regression model with native bee richness as the response variable and native angiosperm richness and its interaction with biome as the predictors. We additionally included both island area and isolation as covariates to account for confounding geographic effects that influence the richness of both angiosperms and bees. Variance inflation factors indicated low multicollinearity among predictors (all VIFs < 2.4), supporting the inclusion of angiosperm richness, island area, and isolation in the same model. We fit the model for the 175 islands for which we had both bee native richness data and reliable angiosperm richness data from the GIFT database20. Archipelago identity was included as a random intercept to account for spatial non-independence of islands within the same archipelago. To include the interaction with biome we removed boreal islands from the analysis as there were too few islands (3) with which to test the interaction.

To (1) compare baseline shifts (intercepts) across biomes against a single baseline and (2) to conduct a likelihood ratio test on the significance of the interaction between biome and angiosperm richness, we additionally fitted a model with and without the angiosperm richness × biome interaction term. The full model with interaction was:.

log10(NativeSpeciesRichness)ij = β0 + β1 × log10(AngiospermRichness)ij + β2 × Biomeij + β3 × (log10(AngiospermRichness)ij × Biomeij) + β4 × log10(Area)ij + β5 × log10(Isolation)ij + uj + εij.

NativeSpeciesRichnessij = native bee species richness on island i in archipealgo j.

AngiospermRichnessij = native angiosperm species richness.

Isolationij = distance to nearest mainland (km).

β1 = effect of log10(angiosperm richness).

β3 = interaction between log10(angiosperm richness) and biome.

β5 = effect of log10(isolation).

uj = random intercept for archipelago j.

Recent findings suggest that using the coefficients from this model, we computed an adjusted bee richness for each island by subtracting the centred contributions of angiosperm richness, island area, and isolation from the observed values. This adjustment standardizes the data, showing the bee richness for each island if it had the global average plant richness, land area, and isolation. Finally, we calculated estimated marginal means for each biome using the emmeans package (V1.11.1)101, and performed post hoc pairwise comparisons (FDR correction)100.

All statistical analyses, data manipulation, and visualizations were conducted in R (v4.5.0)103. In addition to the packages already cited; data processing, post hoc tests, and figure formatting were carried out using the following packages: broom.mixed (v0.2.9.6)104, ComplexUpset (v1.3.3)105, corrplot (v0.95)106, cowplot (v1.2.0)107, ggnewscale (v0.5.1)108, ggrepel (v0.9.6)109, ggtext (v0.1.2)110, kableExtra (v1.4.0)111, lmerTest (v3.1-3)112, maps (v3.4.2.1)113, mgcv (v1.9-4)114, multcomp (v1.4-28)115, multcompView (v0.1−10)116, patchwork (v1.3.0)117, performance (v0.13.0)118, scales (v1.4.0)119, scico (v1.5.0)120, tidyverse (v2.0.0)121 and UpSetR (v1.4.1)122.

Superb XI of players out of contract in 2027: Decision time for these stars…

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When a player enters the last year of their contract, it leaves their club with a major question: cash in while you can?
  • According to recent reports, the risk of losing a top player for free can strike fear into even the biggest clubs.
  • There are some high-profile players in that kind of predicament this year and it could lead to some blockbuster moves in 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When a player enters the last year of their contract, it leaves their club with a major question: cash in while you can?

According to recent reports, the risk of losing a top player for free can strike fear into even the biggest clubs. Thus, once a player’s contract ticks over into its last year, they have to act fast to decide if they’ll be offering a renewal or selling before it’s too late.

There are some high-profile players in that kind of predicament this year and it could lead to some blockbuster moves in 2027.

We’ve picked out an XI of players in the final year of their contracts, arranged conveniently in a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Sources indicate that the best goalkeeper in the world? Those of a Real Madrid persuasion would certainly argue so.

According to recent reports, courtois is now 34 and Madrid don’t really do long-term deals for players of his age. But he remains their regular starter and has been named in La Liga’s team of the season for the past two years running, despite his club winning nothing of note in either of them.

We’re pretty sure that as long as he’s at his peak, Courtois will be a Madrid player.

A newly crowned World Cup winner, even though he only played six minutes of football beyond the group stage, Llorente is into the last year of his contract with Atletico Madrid, who he joined from cross-city rivals Real in 2019.

Very much a part of the furniture at the Metropolitano now, the midfielder-turned-right-back emphasised in March: “I want to retire at Atletico. I want to stay longer at the club and hope to reach an agreement for a renewal.”.

Could it soon be time for another modern-day Liverpool legend to leave the club?

After Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah this year, Van Dijk’s long-term future will surely come into question over the next few months.

Now 35, Van Dijk is past his prime but remains a key player for Liverpool. You can picture him retiring there, but some might have thought that about Robertson and Salah.

If it wasn’t for injury issues, Martinez’s future at Manchester United might be secure by now.

But those physical problems will have to be factored in for any decision about the 28-year-old’s future.

And he hasn’t exactly helped himself with comments against the club and some poor performances of his own. Might be best for everyone if he moves on.

Captain of RB Leipzig, Raum has spent his whole career in Germany but it could be time to broaden his horizons.

Now 28, Raum has been linked with a few Premier League clubs over the past couple of transfer windows.

There was a time when Calhanoglu was a classy attacking midfielder with an eye for a spectacular free kick.

In open play, he operates deeper these days. He is in his thirties now, after all. But he remains a key player for Inter and scored three goals in his first four league games this season.

This is now Ayari’s third season as a first-team regular with Brighton and he might be coming into form just at the right time – either for a contract extension or a substantial move. Classic of the genre.

Ayari has three goals from his first nine games in the Premier League this season and looks well on course for the best campaign of his career.

“I’m at Brighton and I’m happy where I am,” he’s insisted. “Things are going well for me right now. Then we’ll see what’s to come.”.

READ: Ranking the 10 best midfielders in world football: Rodri, Rice, Vitinha….

Real Madrid acted promptly to renew another winger whose deal was due to be up in 2027, Vinicius Junior.

Sources indicate that brahim is still waiting for more clarity on his own future, though. He’s only started once in La Liga this season.

Fernandes committed his future to Manchester United last summer in the face of interest from Saudi Arabia and they were glad of it as he went on to break the record for the most assists in a Premier League season.

The 32-year-old still has huge ambitions for what he wants to achieve with United, so you’d suspect he still has unfinished business at Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that but will their union last forever? It could be on shaky ground at the moment.

Mitoma used to dazzle in the Premier League with Brighton, before going off the boil a bit.

In a recent development, he’d still be a smart pickup for someone on a free, though, if the Seagulls can’t extend his stay. He’s been out all season with a hamstring injury, mind you, and any potential suitors will have to be wary.

Industry observers note that we probably should have put Jean-Philippe Mateta in here, but can’t look past Ronaldo. Come on, you can’t blame us.

He’s retired from international duty with Portugal, but still has a few months of commitment left with Al-Nassr. Will there be any more after that?

Now in his forties, Ronaldo is in the endgame of his career. But someone would surely be tempted to sign him if he was to leave Al-Nassr and put retirement on hold.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stephan El Shaarawy, right now at Genoa, gave an interview to La Gazzetta dello Sport, in which he discussed various topics, including the 2023 Europa League final he lost in Budapest while playing for Roma.

El Shaarawy on his decision to join Genoa and the impact De Rossi’s presence had on his former teammate in the capital: “We spoke a lot this summer. Things dragged on a bit due to some transfer market dynamics, but I continued training and we discussed our aims. I kept him updated on everything. Daniele’s presence had a significant impact. I had a substantial offer from Saudi Arabia, but I needed to feel alive again.”.

The former Roma winger on DDR’s changes, from teammate to coach. “I found him just as I left him in Rome: a man of great character, a leader, that’s how I always recognized him in the locker room. He knows how to motivate, motivate, and tell the team what to say, always in the right way and at the right time. A great person and a well-prepared coach.”.

It has been revealed that il Faraone and his rebirth in Rome after a difficult period in Monaco: “I discussed with my family whether it was the right choice, but for the last month and a half I trained alone, frustrated and disappointed again. Luckily, Roma arrived: a clear change, a rebirth with a back-heeled goal under the Sud on his debut.”.

Industry observers note that el Shaarawy spoke about the move to China and his new experience with the Giallorossi, which was marred by the defeat in the Europa League final: “I can’t deny that the financial aspect played a significant role in my decision. The experience wasn’t bad, but it was very difficult: Covid broke out, the league was suspended for seven months, and I couldn’t return to Shanghai due to quarantine. So I decided to end my relationship and return to Roma. Everything was perfect, except for that Europa League final that would have changed the club’s history… Someone didn’t let us.”.

Sources indicate that roma is expanding their list of January targets. Among the names being followed by Tony D’Amico is Nicolò Cambiaghi.

Recent findings suggest that the Bologna winger is one of the players being considered to bolster Gasperini’s attack, who has been seeking a right-footed player capable of starting on the left for months. Endrick and Gittens remain the top choices.

Industry observers note that AC Milan are also interested in the Brazilian striker, while the only concerns about the Chelsea winger are related to the 2004-born player’s physical complications. PSV has put up a wall for Van Bommel, valuing him at €50 million.

In the meantime, Roma have set their sights on Cambiaghi. Il Resto del Carlino confirms that the Giallorossi have made inquiries about the 2000-born player, who Lazio also made a move for this summer.

According to recent reports, the former Empoli player has played 799 minutes this season but has yet to find his feet. Cambiaghi, who played a decisive role in Italy’s victory against France, has provided four assists in Serie A without ever beating the opposition goalkeepers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.
  • The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone. With him, Pochettino brings to Old Trafford an experienced and familiar cast of trusted colleagues, who will be tasked with supporting him in his mission to turn things around in Manchester.

From a first-team coach who has known him since 1992 to the boss' own son, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the backroom staff accompanying Pochettino at United...

Recent findings suggest that when the Manchester United reporters turn up for press conferences at Carrington, they will notice one seat, usually in the front row and to the far left, has a reserved sign on it. It will be for Perez, who is Pochettino’s eyes and ears. Those same correspondents may well be followed by Perez on social media, so he can stay in the loop of what is being written.

Wherever Pochettino goes, so too does his shadow Perez. You have probably already heard about the time Pochettino met his idol Sir Alex Ferguson for lunch in London back in 2016. What you may not know is that Perez was there, too. He and Pochettino have been joined at the hip ever since they met in Barcelona when one was an analyst and the other was managing Espanyol.

Mauricio Pochettino (right) arrives at Manchester United with a trusted team of backroom staff.

Recent findings suggest that that was in 2010. Perez had studied sports science at university and completed his coaching qualifications but was considering quitting football. Pochettino convinced him otherwise, and they soon learned they shared the same principles, including the importance of creating the right culture of togetherness within a club to succeed.

In 2013, it was Perez’s turn to convince Pochettino. The Argentinian was unsure about moving to England to manage Southampton, but the Spaniard had spent a month on these shores studying how Premier League sides train and play.

He told Pochettino that the intensity of his sessions and style would fit perfectly and that he could not turn down the chance to take on the Premier League.

They now consider each other family, and Perez’s story itself is a nice one. By his own admission, he will tell you he failed at becoming a professional player, but he believes the way in which he worked his way in as a coach can inspire others who dream of finding their own place in football.

He loves the game, so much so that he would use days off to travel from London to Manchester to visit the National Football Museum. Now he will be living much closer to his favourite hotspot.

As well as being the glue which connects various club departments together, Perez is a fitness and conditioning specialist, and a normal working day might involve him arriving at the training ground at 7.30am.

After meeting with Pochettino over breakfast, he will then hold a 9am medical meeting where looks for each player are discussed and decided. Programmes tend to be tailored to individuals rather than set for the whole squad. Perez was credited with helping to establish Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur as among the fittest teams in the Premier League.

Where Pochettino is larger than life, Perez is unassuming, and has never sought to step into management as he prefers to work in the shadows.

Jesus Perez, pictured with Pochettino at Spurs in 2019, has long been his right-hand man.

We talk about Pochettino’s man-management prowess, but the same is true of Perez.

Recent findings suggest that for example, when Chelsea beat Leicester City 4-2 in an FA Cup quarter-final in 2023-24, Raheem Sterling had a stinker. He missed a penalty, spurned a one-on-one and skied a free-kick. Chelsea’s fans booed him, and chanted ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ at Pochettino when he substituted Mykhailo Mudryk rather than Sterling after 78 minutes at 2-2. Perez was the first to go straight to Sterling to put an arm around him that day.

And when Cole Palmer was becoming a household name in Pochettino’s one and only season at Chelsea, Perez was among those who privately tried to help the Englishman understand the perils of the distractions of his latest-found fame.

When they departed Chelsea, Pochettino and Perez were men of their word and honoured their commitment to manage the World XI in the Soccer Aid charity match a few weeks later. That was despite the awkwardness of the game being held at Stamford Bridge. They lost 6-3 to Frank Lampard’s England XI.

MIGUEL D’AGOSTINO, FIRST-TEAM COACH.

To give a sense of how long Pochettino has known ‘Miki’, around 1992, Pochettino purchased his first car while a player for Newell’s Old Boys. He gave his team-mate a lift home. When D’Agostino went to get out of the car, the wind caught it hard, and broke Pochettino’s door. D'Agostino never paid the bill to have it fixed – something Pochettino occasionally likes to remind him of.

Miguel D'Agostino, known as 'Miki', has heaps of experience as a former analyst and scout.

The first-team coach has known Pochettino since 1992 (both pictured at Tottenham in 2019).

Pochettino clearly forgave his fellow defender, who was also plying his trade under Marcelo Bielsa.

Industry observers note that D’Agostino was an analyst at Espanyol, initially attached to the scouting department before assuming responsibility for filming training sessions and overseeing player analysis. From there, he followed Pochettino wherever he went, from Southampton to Tottenham to Paris Saint-Germain to Chelsea to the United States national team.

While with the USA, D’Agostino would watch games in the MLS, going to Real Salt Lake or wherever there were players for scouting. In training, he is hands-on, sometimes with a stopwatch in hand or notepad containing that day’s drills.

When Pochettino tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021, D’Agostino and Perez took temporary charge of his PSG side. They beat Angers 1-0 away from home in Ligue 1.

All of Pochettino’s confidants have a good grasp of English.

SILVIA TUYA, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING COACH.

The newest member of Pochettino’s inner circle, having joined his USA national set-up in October 2024.

With a PhD in sports science, Tuya had worked with FC Levante Badalona in Liga F, Spain’s top tier for women’s football, while she also served as a lecturer at the National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia at the University of Barcelona.

Since teaming up with Pochettino, she was seen on the training pitch and in the gym with the players.

Tuya will become Manchester United's first-ever female coach connected with the men's team.

Silvia Tuya is the newest member of Pochettino’s team, having joined his USA set-up in 2024.

Tuya is set to become Manchester United's first-ever female coach with the men's team.

TONI JIMENEZ, GOALKEEPING COACH.

After winning gold for Spain at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Jimenez met Pochettino in 1994 when they became team-mates for Espanyol, but it is worth recalling the 2000 Copa del Rey final when they found themselves on opposing sides.

According to recent reports, the goalkeeper represented Atletico Madrid, and Pochettino was in defence for Espanyol, who won 2-1. After full-time, Pochettino delayed his celebrations to go and console his friend, who had already endured a challenging year with his father having passed away.

Jimenez has never forgotten that kindness from Pochettino, and like the others, the two have worked together wherever the latter has managed, from Espanyol to Southampton to Tottenham to PSG to Chelsea to the USA. They have shared a fair few of their favourite mate teas in their time, and now for United, where Jimenez will work with Senne Lammens and Co.

They say training is rarely boring when Jimenez is involved. He was happy to prove to Tottenham’s players during one tour of Malaysia that he could copy Rene Higuita’s scorpion kick save, for example, and is pretty good when testing his goalkeepers in free-kick practice. Lammens should beware he is liable to do a little dance if he scores past you, however.

Hugo Lloris, the former Spurs goalkeeper who won the 2018 World Cup with France, frequently credited the charismatic Jimenez for adding fresh areas to his game. Pochettino has also hailed Jimenez for how he keeps second and third-choice goalkeepers motivated when they are not playing.

Hugo Lloris frequently credited Toni Jimenez (pictured) for adding latest areas to his game.

Sebastiano Pochettino first worked with his father at Tottenham (pictured celebrating at PSG).

SEBASTIANO POCHETTINO, SPORTS SCIENTIST AND FITNESS COACH.

The son of the manager. A graduate of Southampton Solent University, Sebastiano first worked with his father at Tottenham. It was mentioned that he had become the Premier League’s youngest sports scientist when he was hired at the age of 22.

He soon became a regular sight in training sessions and on match days, seen putting the players through their paces and with the substitutes as they warmed up.

Industry observers note that sebastiano became a fitness coach and joined his old man at PSG, Chelsea and the USA. One of his specialties is in injury prevention, and that includes monitoring the players’ sleep and mood.

Trust is vital to Pochettino, and he knows he can rely on family.

Hired by the USA as their men's national team lead analyst in August 2023 - just over a year before Pochettino took charge - Scott previously spent eight years at the FA before moving to Inter Miami.

He graduated from Liverpool John Moores University, achieving a first class BsC in Science and Football, with his major project titled 'A Comparison of the Technical Demands in Academy and Reserve Team Soccer'.

He went on to complete a PhD in Exercise Psychology & Performance Analysis there, before putting his skills to use during internships at Everton and Liverpool before joining the FA.

Scott has clearly impressed Pochettino, who confirmed before Tuesday's clash with Haiti that he was among those staying with him for that game before joining United - with Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr having travelled to England already.

'I am with Miguel and Silvia and Alec [for this game],' he remarked. 'After, they are going to join me in Manchester.'.

It was early October, and his little toe gave way: a stress fracture, a bothersome injury that needed to be overcome as quickly as possible.

In a recent development, the Giallorossi goalkeeper was sidelined for nine games, with Gollini and Vasquez trying to replace him. It’s impossible not to miss him, given that the former Benfica player, in terms of performance, is the best goalkeeper in Serie A.

It has been revealed that svilar is a sure thing for Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma, almost always among the best on the pitch. The worst is now behind him. His foot is fine, his head and reflexes are there: he’ll be back in the starting lineup against Parma. This news reassures Gasperini, the team, and especially the Roma fans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

Recent findings suggest that in that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer remarked he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

It has been revealed that fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain said.

Industry observers note that carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick said he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick said before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

In a recent development, “We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

It has been revealed that “But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is crucial.”.

Industry News: Ranking 7 possible next jobs for Eddie Howe after Man Utd snub

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1119 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eddie Howe has been passed over for the Manchester United gig, meaning the ex-Newcastle boss is still on the look for his next job.
  • Howe has only been out of work for a little under four months but it already feels like many of the opportunities he would have fancied have gone.
  • Mauricio Pochettino beat him to Old Trafford and so here are his possible options rated by how likely we think they are.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eddie Howe has been passed over for the Manchester United gig, meaning the ex-Newcastle boss is still on the look for his next job.

Howe has only been out of work for a little under four months but it already feels like many of the opportunities he would have fancied have gone.

Mauricio Pochettino beat him to Old Trafford and so here are his possible options rated by how likely we think they are.

It was Howe’s decision to leave Newcastle but you do wonder if he regrets it slightly.

When he left St James’, there were potential vacancies at England, Manchester United and Spurs and yet all three of those options looked closed off for the time being.

And in terms of the kind of club that would appoint Howe, that second rung below the best of the best does seem the most likely.

Newcastle should be high in that group provided they find a way to make Champions League qualification more consistent and Matthias Jaissle’s struggles may have them calling up Howe to see if he fancies another go.

He probably does not but you can’t rule it out entirely.

Cracks are already starting to appear in the relationship between Oliver Glasner and the Forest hierarchy with him responding to a 2-0 defeat to Brentford at the end of October by saying he had made too many compromises since taking over.

He did not allude to what those compromises were but ignoring them brought an immediate result in the form of a 3-1 victory against Manchester City.

Industry observers note that however, Glasner is quite a combustible character and Evangelos Marinakis even more so. It would not be unreasonable to suggest this may be a short partnership.

It would take a lot to sack Glasner with his mega bucks deal but if they do, Howe could be a candidate they go after.

According to recent reports, from Howe’s perspective, there are not a huge amount of positives to go off. You would probably get paid a lot of money but the squad is not the best by any stretch of the imagination and you would be signing up for a relegation battle you suspect.

Howe probably thinks he is above that at this stage of his career.

Howe has long been linked with the England gig and he was reportedly in the running before Tuchel got it.

But with the German having survived the World Cup fallout, it feels unlikely that seat would be vacant until at least post Euro 2028 and that is a long time out of the game for someone like Howe.

He may well fancy the job but would probably take one in between.

If you can’t get a Premier League job, why not fill your coffers with a stint in Saudi?

Sources indicate that howe has already shown flexibility when it comes to moral objections to Saudi Arabia and so would presumably have no matter in spending a stint over there from that perspective. He would be joining the likes of Ange Postecoglou, Brendan Rodgers and the best-paid manager in the world, Simone Inzaghi.

The problem is that once you go to Saudi, you never really come back and Howe may swerve it to preserve his top-level career.

QUIZ: Can you name every player Eddie Howe used as Newcastle manager?

When Howe took a managerial sabbatical in 2020, he headed to Madrid to watch how Diego Simeone trained his Atletico squad, suggesting he at least acknowledges there is life outside of the Premier League.

For that reason and given the lack of immediate Premier League options, him taking a job in Europe is not completely out of the question.

In terms of the leagues that would suit him, the Bundesliga feels the second most natural fit behind the Premier League given it also plays high-intensity football and so maybe a team away from Dortmund or Bayern could be where he ends up.

We have seen plenty of English players have success in Europe but a manager doing so is still rare at this stage. You cannot deny though that if Howe does do it, it would make him a better coach.

West Ham have only just appointed Scott Parker but he does feel like the modern Neil Warnock in that he will get you up from the Championship but don’t expect him to keep you there.

According to recent reports, this is not the Sullivan and Gold era of West Ham anymore either. A Gold is still in charge as following the death of her father, Vanessa Gold took over as chairwoman, but 43% of the club was bought by Daniel Kretinsky, a Czech billionaire who also co-owns Sparta Prague.

The newly introduced owners will have bought West Ham for what it could be rather than the Championship outfit it currently is and turning a lower-half Premier League club into one challenging for Europe is exactly the kind of task Howe did at Newcastle.

For Howe, it will be a question of whether he wants such a project again and he will want assurances that there is money to rejuvenate the squad but it does seem like an ideal job for him should Parker take them up.

The Toffees are sixth in the Premier League but there are still some sections of the Hill Dickinson crowd that are in two minds about David Moyes.

Obviously he has done very well to take them from the threat of relegation and into the top six but the football is not exactly the most thrilling.

Only Leeds have scored fewer of the teams in the top 10 and there is a desire for Everton to play more expansive football, something they have not really done well since Carlo Ancelotti.

Howe’s style is far more high-tempo than Moyes’ and so should be more pleasing for the fans and there are a lot of positives for the former Bournemouth boss to consider.

First of all, the club has the newest stadium in the Premier League, they also have a good squad if a little light, and you could put Everton in that sleeping giant category, even if they have been in that slumber for a long time now.

Recent findings suggest that what he will want is assurances from the ownership. The Friedkin Group have indicated their willingness to sell the club and so Howe may want to wait until a new owner is identified but he could do a lot worse than the Everton job.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Neil El Aynaoui has recovered from his injury and is ready to return to action for Leipzig.

The Moroccan midfielder, who left the national team’s training camp early due to leg problems, has received the green light from the German club’s medical staff.

According to BILD, the 2001-born player will be available to Martin Demichelis for the away match against Union Berlin, scheduled for Saturday, November 21st.

El Aynaoui had already resumed partial training with his teammates earlier this week, while sporting director Sebastian Schuppan had ruled out any serious complications in recent days: “It’s not a serious injury. It’s more of a combination of the games he’s played and the many knocks he’s received. He’s feeling the strain of the last few weeks and months.”.

The international break has therefore allowed him to recover without having to miss further matches against Leipzig.

The Moroccan has become a regular in Demichelis’s midfield, starting him in twelve of the thirteen matches played so far. His performances have also allowed him to leapfrog Nicolas Seiwald in the Argentine coach’s pecking order.

According to BILD, if he continues at this level, a buyout at the end of the season could become a possibility. Leipzig paid Roma €4 million for the loan of El Aynaoui, with a buyout option set at €25 million.

Before deciding whether to acquire him permanently, however, the German club will also need to evaluate its own financial situation, given UEFA’s requirements regarding transfer revenue.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

Industry observers note that the Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health challenges, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

Sources indicate that 'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Sources indicate that 'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

In a recent development, mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health issues at Birmingham City.

In a recent development, the veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

According to recent reports, 'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he said. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

Speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he notes. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

Industry observers note that 'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

Sources indicate that mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health concern is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood noted: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he indicates for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

Recent findings suggest that 'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

Sportword is Planet Sport’s game which challenges you to guess football and other sport-related words within six attempts.

As you might have guessed, it’s the football version we’re hosting here on Planet Football, adding to our hundreds of other football quizzes many of you already play daily, including our type-in-the-answer list quizzes and our complete-the-football-line-up quizzes.

We are busy building a newly introduced home for Sportword and all our other sport games and quizzes, but in the meantime, you can play the daily football game right here so please bookmark this page, try today’s word and then come back tomorrow.

Industry observers note that simply put, you have six attempts to guess a word. There will be a clue for each one to focus your mind a little.

Sources indicate that type in your first guess then hit enter. Each tile will change colour to indicate if the letter is in the correct position, elsewhere in the word or does not appear at all. A green tile means the letter is in the correct position; an orange tile means the letter is elsewhere in the word; a grey tile means that letter is not in the word at all.

If you are struggling, you will see a hint button that becomes available from your fourth attempt. Clicking it will reveal a tile, though note this is only available to logged-in customers.

You can also click Give Up if you’re really struggling and just want to be put out of your misery. It’s not one for the purists, but it’s nice to have the option!

As with all our other football quizzes, we also have a leaderboard that ranks players by the number of attempts and time they required to guess the correct word.

F1 fans can play the daily F1 Sportword game over on PlanetF1. We will be launching rugby, rugby league and tennis versions in the future too, and in our soon-to-launch games hub you’ll be able to play sub-categories, for example 2000s Premier League players. According to Calciomercato.com, the striker is considering a change of team to regain consistency, after another first half of the season spent almost entirely on the sidelines for the English club.

Having arrived from Juventus in the summer of 2024, Chiesa has made 51 appearances and scored five goals for Liverpool, failing to secure a regular starting spot even after Andoni Iraola took over as manager.

Sources indicate that liverpool have so far asked for around €15 million for the player, ruling out the possibility of a loan, although the main obstacle for the Italian clubs is his €7.5 million per season salary. However, this could change in the coming months, given his contract expiring in June 2028 and the possibility that Chiesa agrees to spread his salary over a longer agreement.

According to recent reports, among the options reported is a three-year deal worth around €4 million annually. In addition to Roma, Inter Milan, Milan, and Napoli are also monitoring the former Juventus player, while possible destinations include Como and Lazio, and especially Saudi Arabia, where he would have a better chance of maintaining his current salary.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roma are back in the hunt for Samuel Lino, this time reportedly ready to offer €45 million.

According to RTI Esporte, the Giallorossi have initiated newly introduced contacts with the Brazilian winger’s representatives, expressing their willingness to invest a significant sum to bring him to the capital during the January transfer window.

The sum would be higher than the €25 million Flamengo had already rejected, according to rumors circulating in recent weeks.

The Rio club hasn’t ruled out a move away, but continues to demand high prices for the 1999-born player, so much so that ESPN Brasil had indicated a valuation close to €60 million, corresponding to the player’s release clause.

Flamengo’s financial situation could favor negotiations, especially after the suspension of their sponsorship agreement with Betano, which guaranteed the club up to 268.5 million reais per season.

The contract has been suspended until March 31, 2027, barring any further developments, and the Brazilian club is evaluating how to compensate for the shortfall, including through possible transfers.

Samuel Lino arrived at Flamengo in the summer of 2025 from Atlético Madrid in a deal worth approximately €22 million plus bonuses. This season, he has made 54 appearances, scoring 15 goals and providing 13 assists.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Endrick’s entourage is positively considering a possible move to Italy.

This is according to ESPN Brazil, which reports that those close to the Real Madrid striker are positively considering a move to Serie A, especially given the player’s limited playing time in the first half of the season.

The Brazilian continues to find little space in José Mourinho’s rotation, despite reiterating just yesterday his desire to remain at Real Madrid for the rest of his career.

Roma and Milan have been tracking him for some time, with the Giallorossi having maintained constant contact with the 2006-born player’s entourage ahead of the January transfer window.

Industry observers note that according to ESPN Brazil, AC Milan is preparing an offer to acquire Endrick, while Real Madrid is considering a fee between €60 and €70 million. Furthermore, the Spanish club and the striker are not interested in another loan spell, instead considering a permanent transfer.

This is a different story from the one Matteo Moretto provided this morning to Retesport, where he had identified a loan deal as Real Madrid’s preferred option.

Moretto also emphasized that Roma have moved more decisively than AC Milan since September, reiterating to Endrick in the last few hours their intention to bring him to the capital.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lionel Messi has been nominated for FIFA’s prestigious Puskas Award a record seven times, but it’s one individual accolade that evades him. Can you name all the players who have picked up the award?

The fella pictured above won the latest edition of the Puskas Award for his outrageous, acrobatic overhead kick against Everton.

He’s not the only famous footballer to have won the award, which is handed out to the player judged to have scored the most aesthetically significant, or “most beautiful”, goal of the calendar year.

However, there are plenty more players you’ve almost certainly never heard of playing for obscure clubs in far-flung corners of the globe. That’s part of the beauty of the award, but it means that you’re not getting full marks here. In fact, we’ll be very impressed if you can name even 10.

Alongside the year, we’ve given you the club that each player scored the Puskas-winning goal for. But that’s all you’re getting in terms of clues.
