#1663. Breaking: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 41m • 📚 Deep Dive (8142 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 41 min read (8142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~41 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2. This is theorized to happen through common envelope evolution (CEE)3, when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag4,5. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, which originates from the CEE of an approximately 7M⊙ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as an approximately 0.7M⊙ companion inspiralling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven-year period of gradual brighteningone of the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. This phase is radiatively efficient, consistent with predictions for convective transport in CEE5,6,7,8. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core powers the ejection of the outermost 10% of the stellar envelope at speeds about 10× the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope4,9,10,11, 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

Industry observers note that near-infrared spectra of AT 2025abao, from its precursor phase (red) and the eruption (blue). The spectra during the precursor phase resemble late M-type stars, while those during the eruption indicates a transition to hotter temperatures. Notably, the CO absorption bands are seen in all spectra, indicating that some molecular gas remains intact even after the eruption.

The black shaded region marks the range expected by varying stellar parameters in the analytical model (section ‘Comparisons to theoretical predictions of enhanced mass loss’). The observed dust mass from the archival progenitor SED and the JWST observation is shown in purple, which constrains the system mass ratio to \(q=0.1{0}_{-0.08}^{+0.10}\).

The mass outflow rate during this phase is  ~10−2 M⊙ yr−1, producing  ~0.1 M⊙ of CBM in an equatorial disk around the binary (dark brown). c, The ballistic eruption in late 2025 from the merger of the inspiraling companion with the primary core, resulting in the ejection of  ≈ 0.1 − 0.2 M⊙ of the primary envelope, and sublimation of a large fraction of dust around the binary. d, The eventual lightcurve powered by shock-interactions between freely expanding merger ejecta (indicated by yellow arrows) and equatorially focused CBM. #1662. Breaking: Remembering when Gazza faced Maradona… & upstaged Diego with a wondergoal

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1141 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Planetfootball ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Remembering when Gazza faced Maradona… & upstaged Diego with a wondergoal

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1141 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paul Gascoigne and Diego Maradona shared something.
  • They were both footballing royalty of course, two of the most wonderfully gifted players of the 1980s and 1990s.
  • It’s something deeper, more fundamental in their make-up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paul Gascoigne and Diego Maradona shared something.

They were both footballing royalty of course, two of the most wonderfully gifted players of the 1980s and 1990s. But it’s not that.

It’s something deeper, more fundamental in their make-up. It’s a level of talent so great that it is seemingly unbearable. Genius, unmistakably, but a genius laden with flaws that were publicly displayed and made them excruciatingly human, that made them relatable and engaging and sometimes hard to watch.

On the one occasion that they faced each other during their professional careers, they shared a laugh in the tunnel before kick-off too.

Lazio travelled to play Sevilla in a friendly in November 1992.

Maradona had rocked in the south of Spain up a few months prior to play under his 1986 World Cup-winning manager Carlos Bilardo after serving a drugs ban that ended his spell at Napoli.

Gascoigne had moved to Lazio from Tottenham at around the same time and was starting to settle in his newly introduced, Roman home.

Industry observers note that yet, for the three days before the friendly, Gascoigne had been on a bender at Disneyland. And on the plane to the Seville, he’d topped himself up with a couple more drinks.

“In the tunnel, I went to Diego: ‘Diego, I’m tipsy,'” Gascoigne told Good Morning Britain in 2020. “He went, “It’s OK, Gazza – so am I.'”.

Inebriated though they were, it wouldn’t stop them putting on a show.

Maradona – scruffy mullet atop his head, gold earring hanging from his left earlobe, portly figure disguised by a very large shirt – was the first to get a chance to display his talents. A free-kick was won, beautifully positioned for his magical left foot, about 25 yards out. It sailed wide.

Then the Argentine showed the game’s first moment of skill, a backheeled pass setting up a half-chance for a Sevilla team-mate. Not long after, Sevilla took the lead. El Diego was not involved, but it was a fine effort, a shot from range by young midfielder Francisco Pineda.

According to recent reports, then Lazio – managed by Dino Zoff and featuring Aron Winter and Giuseppe Favalli – finally got their moment. Of course it came from Gascoigne.

He got the ball back-to-goal, 30 yards out and tightly marked. Too tightly. Gascoigne span his man, evaded another challenge, took a touch to the left, then another to his right. Then it opened up ahead of him and his low, curling shot slipped perfectly into the bottom corner of the net.

Lesser-known Paul Gascoigne goals: for Lazio vs Diego Maradona's Sevilla in 1992, which he claims was immediately after a three-day bender at Disneyland Paris pic.twitter.com/LZSnjFeCOf.

— Adam Hurrey (@FootballCliches) November 10, 2020.

It was a goal Maradona would have been proud to score himself and Gascoigne didn’t miss the chance to rub it in. He told GMB: “I looked at [Maradona] and remarked: ‘Beat that.’ Obviously I spoke to him in Italian, because he doesn’t speak English and neither do I.”.

According to recent reports, maradona would try to beat it, or at least provide his own special something for the fans. But we’ll come to that.

Recent findings suggest that first, as he walked off the pitch at half-time, Maradona was stopped by Spanish television reporters and asked for his thoughts on the game. After answering a generic question about the game being a useful way to keep up match sharpness, he was asked if Gascoigne’s goal had come as a surprise.

“Not at all surprised,” replied a sweaty, breathless Maradona, “he’s a great player. We knew what he could do and he did it to us. We hope that in the second half we can win the game, not just beat Gascoigne.”.

It has been revealed that and it seemed they really did want to win. Certainly, Sevilla’s younger Diego did, Diego Simeone. In the second half, he made a friendly very unfriendly, kicking the legs of, then stamping on the head of, Italian defender Cristiano Bergodi.

If he was trying to rile the Italians, it worked. Simeone, after receiving the ball from Maradona a little later in the half, burst towards the box. He was taken out with a strong, revenge-laced challenge and won another dangerous free-kick. Maradona had the chance to recapture Sevilla’s lead.

This time Diego’s sights were set more accurately than the first. He hit it, sending it curling beautifully over and around the wall. It dropped towards the goal, destined for the top corner… and smacked off the bar.

Sources indicate that disbelief. Maradona shrugged his shoulders, put out his arms, palms facing upwards, and looked at the sky – the sign of a man thinking ‘What more can I do than that?’.

The answer was not much. The referee blew his whistle and the game came to an end. Gascoigne had outshone El Diego, but Maradona had come close to equalling the Englishman’s first-half strike.

In a recent development, of his words of light-hearted provocation aimed at Maradona in the first half, Gascoigne told GMB: “I think I said the wrong thing. Because after that [Maradona] was unbelievable, magic. What a player.”.

As stated earlier, it was the only occasion in their professional careers that the two players faced each other.

Gascoigne was too young for the 1986 World Cup and England only faced Argentina once more during the overlap of their careers, in 1991, with both men missing the game.

READ: The story of the day all three Maradona brothers played for Granada.

Gascoigne might also have caught the end of Diego’s time in Italy had he moved to Lazio a year prior, but again it was not to be, a knee ligament injury in the 1991 FA Cup final with Spurs keeping him out for a season and delaying his transfer.

In a recent development, that their only encounter came in a friendly is a shame. In a competitive match, just imagine what that desire to outdo each other might have produced.

Yet the fact that when they did meet, they were both drunk and both produced moments of magic was a testament to both men’s genius and both men’s flaws.

Sources indicate that in the 2015 Netflix documentary about Gascoigne, Gary Lineker mentioned: “Part of his genius, part of his magnificence is the fact that he is still vulnerable. Without that vulnerable side, I don’t think that he would have been the player that he was.”.

If you were told that same sentence came from the mouth of Jorge Valdano and was about Maradona, you would have no reason to doubt it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

Recent findings suggest that 'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

The Premier League out of contract XI featuring Bruno Fernandes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The January transfer window will soon be upon us, which means a number of clubs will have to decide what to do with their out-of-contract players.
  • January represents the final chance for clubs to recoup any kind of fee before their players leave on a free in the summer, and there are a number of notable Premier League stars with deals set to expire.
  • For now, Alisson is leaving in the summer but the goalkeeper has remarked publicly he wishes to stay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The January transfer window will soon be upon us, which means a number of clubs will have to decide what to do with their out-of-contract players.

January represents the final chance for clubs to recoup any kind of fee before their players leave on a free in the summer, and there are a number of notable Premier League stars with deals set to expire.

For now, Alisson is leaving in the summer but the goalkeeper has remarked publicly he wishes to stay.

He has been at Anfield for eight years, solidifying a previous position of weakness for the club, and has a shout for being the best Premier League goalkeeper of all time.

But he is 34 now and does look less mobile than in earlier years.

He’s on £250k a week, the best-paid goalkeeper in the league, and Liverpool may want to get that off their wage bill but Alisson’s case is helped by the lack of an obvious replacement.

Caoimhin Kelleher was sold to Brentford while Giorgi Mamardashvili has not overly impressed in the chances he has been given.

The Bournemouth stalwart is out of contract this summer having joined 13 years ago.

The Cherries did have his replacement last season in Alex Jimenez but had to drop their new signing for off-field concerns. He was loaned to Fiorentina while Bournemouth brought in Juanlu Sanchez but he has played just 18 minutes of football so far.

This has led to 35-year-old Smith being first choice in the team.

The club captain signed a one-year extension last summer but there is presently no talk of another new deal.

Depending on who you believe, Van Dijk is either close to signing a new deal or has one foot out the door.

The Liverpool skipper’s contract expires at the end of the season and no one is 100% sure if either club or player are looking to extend the relationship.

Van Dijk is still a commanding presence in Liverpool’s back line but is 35 now and is on £350k a week, the second-highest wage in the Premier League.

Liverpool would likely offer only another 12 months and so maybe Van Dijk will seek a fresh challenge at a club willing to offer him longer.

There are a whole host of centre-backs out of contract in the summer with Dan Burn, Calvin Bassey, Joe Gomez, Fabian Schar, Ben Davies, Michael Keane and Chris Richards all approaching the end but perhaps the most interesting one to watch is Lisandro Martinez.

Having criticised United’s director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of recruitment, Martinez may well find himself heading out the door to make room for those improvements.

The club do have the option to extend the deal past the summer but are reportedly in two minds about it considering the outburst. The future of the player will likely depend on Mauricio Pochettino’s view of him.

26% of Palace’s squad is out of contract in the summer, which does not seem the best of planning.

One of the most notable is first-choice left-back Tyrick Mitchell, who is reportedly on the radar of Manchester United and Liverpool.

Industry observers note that palace have the option of extending it a further 12 months but are right now in talks to tie him down to a new deal. Failure to do that and Palace could have another Guehi situation on their hands in the near future.

Ayari is coming towards the end of the four-and-a-half-year deal he signed to first join Brighton back in 2023, although the club do have the option to extend it for a further year.

Contract talks over a upcoming deal are not going well apparently, with Ayari yet to commit to anything as he wishes to keep his options open.

The standout performer of the season so far only returned to Brighton in January and penned an 18-month deal with his former club.

That seemed a wise move for a player who will be 36 come the end of it but his current form makes the option of an extension hard to ignore.

If Brighton, who usually have these things planned out, do offer him a upcoming deal, you suspect it will be for another 12 months rather than committing to a long-term deal for an ageing player.

Europe’s top 10 chance creators in 2026-27: Yamal, Guler, Olise all trail surprise leader.

Fernandes has reportedly already rejected two offers from United but the club do have the right to extend it for a further 12 months.

However, extending the deal of a player who has indicated a desire to leave would not sit well with Fernandes, who has a lot of political capital at Old Trafford.

As for the player, he is 32 now and one League Cup, one FA Cup, one Portuguese Cup and two Portuguese League Cups is not the kind of trophy cabinet that reflects his ability.

He may fancy moving to a different club, one where trophies are more assured, but United look determined to ensure that does not happen until 2028 at the earliest.

Murphy has been at Newcastle for almost 10 years having been signed by Rafa Benitez, which seems a remarkable fact.

His contract is due to expire in the summer with Everton and Nottingham Forest rumoured to be interested, but a loss of many senior players has reportedly prompted Matthias Jaissle to ask the club to keep hold of Murphy.

The Mail says talks are “accelerating” on a fresh deal and Murphy, despite being 31, is even being offered improved terms.

Having looked to legally get his contract ripped up in the summer, Mateta will have a much easier route out of Selhurst Park in 2027.

Mateta has been eager to leave Palace for a while now, making it as far as an AC Milan medical before a knee injury collapsed that move.

He is back in the Palace squad now, playing four games this season, but has yet to score and has picked up a red card.

He’s a decent Premier League striker with double digits of goals in the last three seasons but at 29 years of age, he will probably not be sought after by the very top end of clubs.

Mitoma has been on the sidelines since May with a hamstring injury that required surgery.

Understandably, the Seagulls are being careful with his rehab and so it is only this weekend that he is thought to be in contention for the squad.

Pre-injury, Mitoma was one of Brighton’s best players but it feels like the team has evolved a lot since then and there is always a bit of doubt over how a player returns from such a lengthy absence.

His contract expires in the summer and there have been rumours of a departure for two years now, with the Japanese international reportedly wanting Champions League football.

But with his injury, a Champions League club may not want to take the risk and the Seagulls could be in the competition themselves next season.

If he comes back and performs well, it is likely you would expect him to extend beyond the summer.
